findings.description: `total = sum(1 for _ in lines)` exhausts `lines` before the main loop runs. The CLI passes an open file object, which is a one-shot iterator. The `for line in lines` loop then sees no lines, so read/written stay 0 and the output file is empty. Progress reports 0/total.
findings.suggestion: Avoid the pre-count (report progress without a total), or materialise the lines in a list, or count in a separate pass that reopens or seeks the file.
findings.title: Counting lines consumes a one-shot iterator, so nothing is processed

findings.description: In the `except LookupTimeout` branch the code does `return enrich(event, geo)` without `await`. `enrich_one` therefore returns a coroutine object, which `_flush` passes to `sink`. `to_json` then fails or writes garbage, and the coroutine is never awaited. The retry never actually runs. A second timeout would not abort the run as documented.
findings.suggestion: Use `return await enrich(event, geo)` so the retry runs and a second LookupTimeout propagates.
findings.title: Retry returns an un-awaited coroutine instead of the Event

findings.description: `asyncio.gather` without handling leaves the other tasks running when one raises, so they may continue after the exception propagates. Because the sink is only called after the whole batch completes, a failure discards that batch's results. Earlier batches are already written, so the output file is left partially written.
findings.suggestion: Use `asyncio.TaskGroup`, or cancel the pending tasks on error.
findings.title: Failure in one lookup leaves sibling tasks running and the batch partially handled
